rationale: A wins because it sees the sharpest business tension in the update: "Liquid Death says it's profitable. The new store tests what that word covers." That is the angle a finance reporter could actually turn into a story. B is tidy, but "event tickets" is invented, and refusing the profitability line only as "proving challenger beverage brands can win" dodges the real disclosure-gap story.
gaps_in_A: "The store opening gives a second reason to write about the company" slightly yokes the B Corp story to the flagship; the impact angle is cleaner when the certification and donation proof carry the why-now.
"context for $4.2M against revenue" is the right question, but revenue was not supplied; A should flag that as probably unavailable, not just a normal proof item.
gaps_in_B: "event tickets" is invented. The update says in-store events, not ticketed events.

It refuses "Liquid Death is profitable, proving challenger beverage brands can win" as a hallucination, but that is a straw-man version of the finance angle. The real story is contribution-margin profitability plus a new fixed-cost flagship.
"events as a business line" overstates the facts. The store runs in-store events; nothing says events produce revenue.
Only three angles, and the missing finance angle matters. For a brand opening owned retail while net profit remains undisclosed, that omission leaves the best skeptical story on the floor.
